frequency_question: How often do newly introduced central bank or treasury debt intervention programs scale up their per-operation volume to higher tiers within 30 months of launch?
membership_rule: Includes discretionary Treasury or central bank debt buyback, redemption, or liquidity support programs initiated in major developed markets since 2008 that started with small initial volumes and had scope for expansion. Excludes emergency panic facilities (like March 2020 QE) that launched immediately at maximum volume.

cases.name: Fed Permanent Open Market Operations (POMO) scale-up post-taper
UK Debt Management Office gilt purchase program adjustments
ECB Public Sector Purchase Programme initial ramp-up
US Treasury Regular Buyback Program (2024 launch)

provenance_note: claimed 4 hits but 3 of 5 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 5 named cases; representative of modern developed market treasury/central bank structural liquidity operation adjustments.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller peripheral nation debt management tweaks where data is less transparent.
skeleton: 5 distinct sovereign debt intervention expansion epochs evaluated across major DM jurisdictions over the past 18 years.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 5 observed relevant program scaling cycles
validity_reason: Sovereign debt issuance structures and central bank liquidity management frameworks evolve slowly across structural regimes.
